answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a bond before accepting jobs, caps its unpaid work at that bond, and confiscates the bond when a signed result fails a deterministic check. Like a vine held by a trellis anchored deep in a dune, trust rests on costly support: splitting into a thousand identities creates no extra unsecured capacity. The attacker must tie up capital for every account and loses it for provably invalid work.
